thread:
matthew: heads up — onboarding sample app crashes in a notebook with RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop :thinking_face:
elaine: oh no, can you paste the minimal repro?
matthew: sure, super minimal. run a jupyter cell with this:
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key=\"x\")  # crashes on import/construct in notebook
await client.generate(\"hi\")
```
sam: i bet the ctor is doing sync auth w/ requests or calling asyncio.run internally
ashley: yup saw similar in a sample last week — top-level init doing blocking work is the root cause
matthew: stacktrace (trimmed):
```
RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/async_client.py", line 84, in __init__
    token = self._sync_fetch_token()  # calls requests.post(...)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/async_client.py", line 120, in _sync_fetch_token
    asyncio.run(self._refresh())
```
mike: ouch. That pattern is one of the common footguns for notebooks, uvicorn, and tests. We should avoid any use of asyncio.run in library code
elaine: for immediate workaround you can do:
```python
import nest_asyncio
nest_asyncio.apply()
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key="x")
await client.generate("hi")
```
elaine: but we definitely shouldn't recommend nest_asyncio in our quickstart
sam: proposal: add an async factory like `await AsyncClient.create(...)` that does async auth, and make __init__ lazy (no network calls). Also provide a sync helper `SyncClient.from_api_key(...)` for sync quickstarts
ashley: agree. also update the notebook quickstart to use the factory pattern explicitly and call it out in the onboarding checklist
mike: +1. can we also avoid hiding implicit background tasks? prefer library to require explicit start/stop or context manager
matthew: what about a migration shim? keep old ctor but emit DeprecationWarning and schedule patch for next minor release
infra-bot: issue created: DEVEX-2109 — \"AsyncClient ctor does blocking auth; add AsyncClient.create and lazy init\" (assign to @mike) :white_check_mark:
ashley: i'll open the sample-app PR to switch quickstart notebook to `client = await AsyncClient.create(...)` and update the README steps. will link the PR to DEVEX-2109
sam: tiny API nit: name it `create` vs `init`; `create` signals coroutine/factory better than `init` in my opinion
mike: agreed. implementation notes:
- make __init__ accept `auth_token=None` and store params only
- implement `@classmethod async def create(cls, *, api_key=None, base_url=None):`
- move existing token refresh logic into async methods only
- add contextmanager `async with AsyncClient.create(...) as client:` to ensure cleanup

matthew: can we also add a linter rule or test that imports sample apps under pytest-asyncio to catch this class of regressions early? i hit this during onboarding, so it would help others
elsie: (cc @elaine) small docs tweak: under quickstart call out "do not call client constructors at module import time" with a one-line example
elaine: sounds good — i'll draft the docs patch after the sample-app PR lands. thanks everyone for the quick feedback :raised_hands:
mike: i'll take DEVEX-2109, follow up with design PR, and add a short migration guide to the changelog for the fix. target next week for the sample app fix and release patch.
matthew: thanks — this was blocking a new hire onboarding flow, so great to get it triaged quickly :thumbsup:
